title: Token Counts Are Not Model Lineage: A Frozen-Threshold Holdout Study of Black-Box LLM API Fingerprinting
abstract: arXiv:2608.29930v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Black-box model attribution is increasingly relevant when large language models (LLMs) are served through relay and reseller APIs. A tempting low-cost signal is the prompt-token count returned by an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: two models that share a tokenizer and chat template may produce the same count sequence up to a fixed offset. Yet the validity of this signal for broader \emph{model-family} attribution has received little direct holdout testing. We conduct a frozen-threshold study over 24 labeled endpoint pairs, split evenly into a development set and an untouched holdout set, with three temporal repeats and 30 controlled texts per pair. We introduce a validity-gated result contract that distinguishes an observed dissimilarity from an uninformative measurement caused by missing usage data, rate limits, or endpoint policy. translated_title: Token Counts Are Not Model Lineage: A Frozen-Threshold Holdout Study of Black-Box LLM API Fingerprinting
translated_abstract: 当大语言模型（LLM）通过中转和转售 API 提供服务时，黑盒模型归因问题变得日益重要。一个看似诱人的低成本信号是 OpenAI 兼容端点返回的提示词 token 计数：共享分词器和聊天模板的两个模型可能产生仅相差固定偏移量的相同计数序列。然而，该信号在更广泛的模型家族归因上的有效性尚未得到直接的留出集测试。我们对 24 个带标签的端点对开展了冻结阈值研究，将其平均划分为开发集和未触碰的留出集，每个端点对进行三次时间重复实验并使用 30 个受控文本。我们引入了一种有效性门控的结果契约，用于区分真实观测到的差异与由缺失用量数据、速率限制或端点策略导致的无信息测量。所得的平移不变精确匹配分数完美区分了 12 个开发集端点对，并由此得到一个冻结的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文通过冻结阈值的留出集实验和有效性门控结果契约，系统验证了黑盒 LLM API 返回的提示词 token 计数虽能区分开发集模型对，但并不能作为模型谱系（家族）归因的可靠指纹信号。
en_tdlr: A frozen-threshold holdout study with a validity-gated result contract demonstrates that prompt-token counts from black-box LLM APIs can separate development model pairs but are not a reliable fingerprint signal for model-family lineage attribution.
